briar.thomas.first.text: I know that look. You think you're going out there. The Legion is at our fields, and half the village is holding tools instead of weapons.

choices.text: Someone has to keep them away from home.
I'm scared too. But hiding won't stop them.
Then I'd better look dangerous from a distance.

voice.speaker: thomas
voice.direction: Trying to sound firm while quietly frightened for your child. Practical, familiar warmth. No hint about adoption.
voice.context: The Hollowed Legion has reached Briar Town. Your child refuses to hide. You reluctantly help them prepare.

briar.thomas.protect.text: I know. I just wish that someone didn't have to be you. Come here. That strap won't last a minute.

choices.text: Help me get ready.

effects.title: Make room for the wounded
effects.text: Mara needs help treating our neighbors. Find her near the village beds.

voice.speaker: thomas
voice.direction: You understand the need to fight. The pause before asking them closer is a father swallowing his worry.
voice.context: The Hollowed Legion has reached Briar Town. Your child refuses to hide. You reluctantly help them prepare.

briar.thomas.afraid.text: Being scared means you're paying attention. Let me fix your strap. Then promise me you'll come back when you need help.

choices.text: I promise. What's the first thing I can do?

effects.title: Make room for the wounded
effects.text: Mara needs help treating our neighbors. Find her near the village beds.

voice.speaker: thomas
voice.direction: Reassuring rather than grand. Fear is sensible. The promise matters deeply to you.
voice.context: The Hollowed Legion has reached Briar Town. Your child refuses to hide. You reluctantly help them prepare.

briar.thomas.joke.text: Try standing behind the fence. Makes you look taller. Hold still while I fix this strap.

choices.text: Thanks, Dad. Who needs help first?

effects.title: Make room for the wounded
effects.text: Mara needs help treating our neighbors. Find her near the village beds.

voice.speaker: thomas
voice.direction: A small familiar dad joke to hide worry. Return to practical care at the strap.
voice.context: The Hollowed Legion has reached Briar Town. Your child refuses to hide. You reluctantly help them prepare.

briar.thomas.ready.text: Go to Mara. She has wounded people arriving and barely enough supplies for the ones already there. I'll help the neighbors pack. We're not leaving anyone behind.

voice.speaker: thomas
voice.direction: You have accepted they will go. Give clear, useful directions, then steady resolve about the neighbors.
voice.context: The Hollowed Legion has reached Briar Town. Your child refuses to hide. You reluctantly help them prepare.

briar.mara.first.text: Good. Someone still on their feet. I need tangle roots to bring down the fevers and clean dressings for the wounds. We can't move these people safely yet.

choices.text: Tell me where to look.
Will this help us hold the village?
I'm better at finding trouble. Will that do?

voice.speaker: mara
voice.direction: Tired but capable. Busy treating neighbors; glad to see someone who can help. Dry warmth, not despair.
voice.context: Your neighbors are wounded as the Legion reaches the village. Supplies let you treat them and reopen the large healing pad.

briar.mara.why.text: These are our neighbors. Some can help hold the lane once they're treated. The rest need to be well enough to leave it. Both matter.

choices.text: All right. What do you need?

voice.speaker: mara
voice.direction: Explain why caring for ordinary neighbors matters. Compassionate and direct, not a speech.
voice.context: Your neighbors are wounded as the Legion reaches the village. Supplies let you treat them and reopen the large healing pad.

briar.mara.joke.text: Only if it comes wrapped in clean cloth. And please don't bring it inside.

choices.text: Roots and dressings. Where are they?

voice.speaker: mara
voice.direction: A dry joke, delivered while working. A little smile at the end; no slapstick.
voice.context: Your neighbors are wounded as the Legion reaches the village. Supplies let you treat them and reopen the large healing pad.

briar.mara.supplies.text: Three tangle roots from the overgrown garden, and a bundle of clean dressings from the shuttered store. The front is blocked. Look around the back for a way inside.

choices.text: I'll bring them here.

effects.title: Mara’s supplies
effects.text: Find 3 tangle roots in the overgrown garden and clean dressings in the shuttered store. Check the back of the store. Bring both to Mara.

voice.speaker: mara
voice.direction: Clear directions with natural breathing between each location. This is the player’s first delivery request.
voice.context: Your neighbors are wounded as the Legion reaches the village. Supplies let you treat them and reopen the large healing pad.

briar.mara.wait.text: Roots from the garden. Dressings from the store. And if you're thinking of tasting a root, I'd rather not find you a bed.

choices.text: Here are the roots and dressings.

effects.title: Mara’s supplies delivered
effects.text: Mara has treated the wounded and reopened the large healing pad.

effects.title: Healing pads
effects.text: Mara’s large pad heals you fully and never runs out. Small pads have limited healing. Save them for when you need them.

voice.speaker: mara
voice.direction: A useful reminder followed by gentle teasing. Do not sound irritated when the player returns early.
voice.context: Your neighbors are wounded as the Legion reaches the village. Supplies let you treat them and reopen the large healing pad.

briar.mara.heal.text: That's enough. Give me a moment... There. The large healing pad is working again. Stand on it whenever you need to heal. It won't run out. The small pads you'll find out there only hold a little healing, so use them wisely.

choices.text: What should I do next?

effects.title: Open the way out
effects.text: The mill crossing is stuck. Find what is jamming the wheel so the villagers can reach the escape lane.

voice.speaker: mara
voice.direction: Relief at receiving supplies. Brief working pause at “Give me a moment.” Then explain both healing-pad types clearly.
voice.context: Your neighbors are wounded as the Legion reaches the village. Supplies let you treat them and reopen the large healing pad.

briar.mara.next.text: The mill crossing is stuck. Gus was checking the wheel. See what's caught in it, and make a way through. I'll get these people ready to move.

voice.speaker: mara
voice.direction: Focused encouragement. You are staying with the wounded while the player clears the escape route.
voice.context: Your neighbors are wounded as the Legion reaches the village. Supplies let you treat them and reopen the large healing pad.

briar.gus.first.text: I put my best tools in the loft. Safe from thieves, damp, and apparently me. Now the Legion is outside and I can't make my legs climb the ladder.

choices.text: What do you need?
Why stay here?
Scared of your own ladder?

voice.speaker: gus
voice.direction: Dry humor covering real fear. The joke is on yourself, not the people in danger.
voice.context: Briar Town is under attack. Gus is a frightened carpenter trying to keep his neighbors safe. This optional quest never blocks the village escape.

briar.gus.home.text: I built half these doors. Fixed the other half after Thomas tried. These are my neighbors. I'm not leaving them with nowhere to hide.

choices.text: Then let's give them somewhere safe.
You're not helping much down here.

voice.speaker: gus
voice.direction: Warm pride, then embarrassment. Thomas is a familiar friend; tease him kindly.
voice.context: Briar Town is under attack. Gus is a frightened carpenter trying to keep his neighbors safe. This optional quest never blocks the village escape.

briar.gus.request.text: My tool roll is upstairs, by the little window. Bring it down and I can unstick the workshop's back door. There's a narrow way through to the other side. I've got something purple you can have, too. Found it in the roof. Nearly broke my saw.

choices.text: I'll bring your tools back.

effects.title: Gus's good tools
effects.text: Gus left his tool roll in the workshop loft. Bring it back so he can open a safer way through the workshop.

voice.speaker: gus
voice.direction: Practical, relieved to have a plan. Curious about the purple piece, with no knowledge of its origin.
voice.context: Briar Town is under attack. Gus is a frightened carpenter trying to keep his neighbors safe. This optional quest never blocks the village escape.

briar.gus.waiting.text: The roll by the loft window. Please bring the whole thing. Last time someone borrowed my hammer, I got a spoon back.

choices.text: Your tools. All of them.

effects.title: A safer way through
effects.text: Gus opened the workshop shortcut and gave us a Rift Shard. The shortcut is optional; the mill crossing still leads out of town.

voice.speaker: gus
voice.direction: A little lighter now someone has offered help. Let the spoon joke land without exaggerating it.
voice.context: Briar Town is under attack. Gus is a frightened carpenter trying to keep his neighbors safe. This optional quest never blocks the village escape.

briar.gus.thanks.text: Still got all ten fingers? Good. Better than my first week. Here, take the purple piece. I'll get this door open. If the street gets rough, come through my workshop.

choices.text: Keep yourself safe, Gus.

voice.speaker: gus
voice.direction: Genuine gratitude with a small joke. Tools restored; he can contribute again.
voice.context: Briar Town is under attack. Gus is a frightened carpenter trying to keep his neighbors safe. This optional quest never blocks the village escape.

briar.gus.done.text: Door's open. Watch the low beam. It has won every argument I've had with it.

voice.speaker: gus
voice.direction: Warm farewell. Quietly proud to be useful.
voice.context: Briar Town is under attack. Gus is a frightened carpenter trying to keep his neighbors safe. This optional quest never blocks the village escape.

briar.gus.hurt.text: Yes. I'm scared. That sign outside has had our village name on it since I was little. They knocked it into the mud. I couldn't even stand it back up. You don't need to make me feel smaller.

choices.text: The sign is standing again. I should have helped.
I'm sorry. That was unfair.
Maybe hiding is all you're good for.

effects.title: Gus wants to be left alone
effects.text: I pushed Gus too far. He will not offer his tools job this time. The mill crossing is still open to us once it is repaired.

voice.speaker: gus
voice.direction: No comic delivery. Hurt and ashamed, with affection for the village sign. This is the clue to a possible repair.
voice.context: Briar Town is under attack. Gus is a frightened carpenter trying to keep his neighbors safe. This optional quest never blocks the village escape.

briar.gus.sorry.text: All right. I heard you. Just... give me a minute. I hate looking out there and seeing our name in the dirt.

choices.text: I stood the sign back up.

voice.speaker: gus
voice.direction: Apology acknowledged, still bruised. The sign matters to him; do not sound like a quest checklist.
voice.context: Briar Town is under attack. Gus is a frightened carpenter trying to keep his neighbors safe. This optional quest never blocks the village escape.

briar.gus.repair.text: You put it back. Even with all this going on. Thank you. Maybe my legs will remember their job if my hands get to work. Could you fetch those tools?

choices.text: Tell me where they are.

voice.speaker: gus
voice.direction: Surprised warmth. The player acted with care, and his trust begins to return.
voice.context: Briar Town is under attack. Gus is a frightened carpenter trying to keep his neighbors safe. This optional quest never blocks the village escape.

briar.gus.closed.text: Go. I'll find someone else to help. I've got enough trouble outside my door.

voice.speaker: gus
voice.direction: Curt, controlled hurt. Final refusal for this attempt, not a melodramatic threat.
voice.context: Briar Town is under attack. Gus is a frightened carpenter trying to keep his neighbors safe. This optional quest never blocks the village escape.

briar.lewis.first.text: Keep your voice down. Their signal post is ahead. If that horn sounds, every patrol in these woods will know where our neighbors are.

choices.text: How do I get past them?
What are they doing out here?

voice.speaker: lewis
voice.direction: Quiet urgency. You are watching the tree line while helping someone you know.
voice.context: Briar’s neighbors have escaped the fields. Lewis needs the Legion signal stopped so they can cross the woods safely.

briar.lewis.routes.text: The low path runs through their camp. Or climb the roots on the right and cross the old hunting platforms. Stop the crank below the horn, or cut its cable from above. Either works. I would take the high path. My knees voted against it.

choices.text: Keep the others here. I’ll stop the signal.

effects.title: Silence the signal
effects.text: Lewis is keeping the neighbors back. I can stop the signal at its ground crank or climb the eastern roots to cut its upper cable. The northern clearing leads onward.

voice.speaker: lewis
voice.direction: Useful directions, then a small dry joke. Keep the danger believable.
voice.context: Briar’s neighbors have escaped the fields. Lewis needs the Legion signal stopped so they can cross the woods safely.

briar.lewis.prisoners.text: They marched prisoners north, toward Hollow Pass. I saw one guard call a woman by name. She thought he knew her. Then he tied her hands. We cannot let them catch our people.

choices.text: Show me the way to the signal.

voice.speaker: lewis
voice.direction: Controlled anger. A witness describing what happened, not a lore lecture.
voice.context: Briar’s neighbors have escaped the fields. Lewis needs the Legion signal stopped so they can cross the woods safely.

briar.lewis.waiting.text: I’ll keep the neighbors behind us. Once the horn is quiet, use the north clearing. And watch the old platforms. The wood is older than my excuses.

choices.text: The signal is down. Get everyone moving.

voice.speaker: lewis
voice.direction: Steady support. Let the last sentence release a little tension.
voice.context: Briar’s neighbors have escaped the fields. Lewis needs the Legion signal stopped so they can cross the woods safely.

briar.lewis.clear.text: No horn. No patrol rushing after us. That is the best thing I have heard all day. The others are resting here. Something large is blocking the way ahead. I wish that was another joke.

voice.speaker: lewis
voice.direction: Relief first, then sober warning. Keep the last line quiet.
voice.context: The signal is disabled and the neighbors have reached shelter. The Brute still blocks their escape.

briar.beth.first.text: My brother went after the sheep. Then the bridge broke. I heard him shout once. Now all I can hear is those beasts. Please tell me you’re better at climbing than I am.

choices.text: Show me where he went.

effects.title: Nobody left behind
effects.text: Beth’s brother went east after their sheep. Follow the boot prints past the broken bridge. He may be trapped near the old rope lift. This rescue is optional; the signal post is still the main task.

choices.text: He went back for sheep?
Your brother is safe.

voice.direction: Worried, trying to stay steady. Relief should come later.
voice.context: Optional Black Woods rescue. Beth’s brother crossed a broken bridge to save their sheep and was trapped by a fallen tree. Wild beasts block his escape.
voice.speaker: beth

briar.beth.sheep.text: They’re our winter food, our wool, half our living. He wasn’t being foolish. Well, he was being a little foolish. But for a good reason.

choices.text: I’ll look for him.

effects.title: Nobody left behind
effects.text: Beth’s brother went east after their sheep. Follow the boot prints past the broken bridge. He may be trapped near the old rope lift. This rescue is optional; the signal post is still the main task.

choices.text: He is safe now.

voice.direction: Defend him warmly; a tiny rueful smile on the last sentence.
voice.context: Optional Black Woods rescue. Beth’s brother crossed a broken bridge to save their sheep and was trapped by a fallen tree. Wild beasts block his escape.
voice.speaker: beth

briar.beth.trail.text: His boots leave a crooked heel print. Follow them east. The old bridge has a few beams left, and there’s a dry path below if you slip. Please bring him back. I can shout at him myself.

choices.text: He’s free. The crossing is safe now.

voice.direction: Practical directions, then affectionate worry.
voice.context: Optional Black Woods rescue. Beth’s brother crossed a broken bridge to save their sheep and was trapped by a fallen tree. Wild beasts block his escape.
voice.speaker: beth

briar.beth.relief.text: There he is. Both legs. That’s a good start. Our dog has been trying to follow you since you got here. Once we’re safely out of these woods, let him come with you. He knows who keeps people safe.

voice.direction: Deep relief. Brief dry humor; offer the dog with trust, not a sales pitch.
voice.context: Optional Black Woods rescue. Beth’s brother crossed a broken bridge to save their sheep and was trapped by a fallen tree. Wild beasts block his escape.
voice.speaker: beth

briar.bethBrother.first.text: Don’t come straight at the tree! The trunk will roll. That rope lift can take its weight, but those beasts won’t let anyone near it.

choices.text: I’ll clear a path to the rope.
You’re free. Beth’s waiting.

voice.direction: Urgent but clear. He is stuck behind the fallen tree, not mortally wounded.
voice.context: Optional Black Woods rescue. Beth’s brother crossed a broken bridge to save their sheep and was trapped by a fallen tree. Wild beasts block his escape.
voice.speaker: bethBrother

briar.bethBrother.wait.text: I can walk. I just need a way out. Beth is going to be furious. If she asks, this was a very sensible plan until the bridge part.

choices.text: You can get back across now.

voice.direction: Nervous joke. Keep the danger believable.
voice.context: Optional Black Woods rescue. Beth’s brother crossed a broken bridge to save their sheep and was trapped by a fallen tree. Wild beasts block his escape.
voice.speaker: bethBrother

briar.bethBrother.safe.text: You lifted the tree and fixed the crossing? Right. I’m going before you find a third thing I broke. Thank you. Really.

voice.direction: Starts sheepish, ends with sincere gratitude.
voice.context: Optional Black Woods rescue. Beth’s brother crossed a broken bridge to save their sheep and was trapped by a fallen tree. Wild beasts block his escape.
voice.speaker: bethBrother

effects.title: The mill crossing
effects.text: The water is stopped. Look for the timber caught in the wheel beside the mill.

effects.title: The mill crossing
effects.text: The wheel is clear. Use the bridge handle beside the stream to lower the crossing.

effects.title: A way out
effects.text: The crossing is down. Clear the Legion guards at the old stone bridge, then open the wagon gate on the far rise. Thomas will lead the neighbors out.

effects.title: The neighbors are safe
effects.text: Thomas has led the neighbors out. Follow the path into the Black Woods to find where the Legion is coming from.

effects.title: The farm bells
effects.text: The tower stone reads: First the sun wakes us. Then water feeds the fields. Last, wheat fills our tables. Three bells carry those marks.

effects.title: The farm bells
effects.text: The bells opened the old tower chest. We recovered the coins inside.

effects.title: The granary scale
effects.text: The grain keeper left a note: Five sacks balance the old store-room door. The hanging weights are marked one, two and four. I can raise or lower each one with its handle.

effects.title: The granary store room
effects.text: Five balanced the door. The weights are held in place and the store room is open. We recovered the grain keeper’s saved coins.

effects.title: Supplies for Briar
effects.text: I recovered the wagon’s food and bandages. The neighbors will need these on the way out. I also found the driver’s spare coins.

effects.title: The fruit pickers’ walkway
effects.text: The old note says: Raise the walkway when the boars come. The hand wheel is up by the picking platforms. There may still be something in the lookout chest.

effects.title: Above the orchard
effects.text: I lowered the fruit pickers’ walkway. It leads to a lookout beyond the trees. The steps on the far side lead back down.

effects.title: The orchard lookout
effects.text: Someone left their savings in the lookout chest. The walkway and the far steps make a loop back through the orchard.

effects.title: The horn is silent
effects.text: The Legion signal is disabled. The neighbors can move toward the northern shelter. The path beyond leads to the Brute’s approach. I can still explore before leaving this part.

effects.title: The horn is silent
effects.text: The Legion signal is disabled. The neighbors can move toward the northern shelter. The path beyond leads to the Brute’s approach. I can still explore before leaving this part.

effects.title: Tracks around the old stones
effects.text: The carving says: Follow the tracks from the shallow pool to the split tree. Press the matching stones in that order. The prints are still visible along the grove’s western edge.

effects.title: Nobody left behind
effects.text: Beth’s brother went east after their sheep. Follow the boot prints past the broken bridge. He may be trapped near the old rope lift. This rescue is optional; the signal post is still the main task.

effects.title: Nobody left behind
effects.text: Beth and her brother are together at the eastern trail junction. The rope lift has opened a safe crossing. Their shepherd dog will join my companions when I finish Black Woods. I do not need to return to Beth to claim it.
